name: Issachar
description: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: Issachar is the so-called Aztec Indian, the Mexican of today. Issachar is a strong ass: a hard worker, given over to hard work and known over the earth for labor.

note.label: Genesis 49: What Shall Befall the Twelve Tribes in the Last Days

points: On the second day Nethaneel the son of Zuar, prince of Issachar, offered. Each prince on his day brought the very same offering as Nahshon, because this was the order that they had to do.

The twelve days went in the order of the camps: Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Reuben, Simeon, Gad, Ephraim, Manasseh, Benjamin, Dan, Asher, and Naphtali, closing with Ahira the son of Enan on the twelfth day.

note.label: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar

points: Moses charged the people that day: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph (which is Ephraim and Manasseh), and Benjamin were to stand upon mount Gerizim to bless the people.

note.label: Deuteronomy 27: Write the Law upon Stones

points: And of Zebulun he said, Rejoice, Zebulun, in thy going out; and, Issachar, in thy tents. Notice the grouping: Zebulun and Issachar are blessed together because they would dwell very close, with linked cities at their borders.

note.label: Deuteronomy 33: The Blessing of Moses, Identifying the Tribes in the Last Days

points: The coast descended to the river Kanah: southward of the river the cities were Ephraim's, and northward it was Manasseh's, the sea was his border, and they met together in Asher on the north and in Issachar on the east.

note.label: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim

points: Manasseh also had within Issachar and Asher the cities of Beth-shean, Ibleam, Dor, En-dor, Taanach, and Megiddo with their towns, even three countries.

note.label: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim

points: The fourth lot came out to Issachar according to their families, and their border was toward Jezreel; their coast reached to Tabor and went out at Jordan, sixteen cities with their villages.

note.label: Joshua 19: The Portions of the Remaining Tribes

points: The children of Gershon had thirteen cities out of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and the half tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, and the children of Merari had twelve cities out of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun; all given by lot as the Most High commanded by the hand of Moses.

note.label: Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites

points: After Abimelech there arose to defend Israel Tola the son of Puah, a man of Issachar; he judged Israel twenty and three years, and died, and was buried in Shamir.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: The twelve sons of Israel are set down: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

points: The Levites had no land inheritance like the rest of the tribes, so these cities and their suburbs are where they dwelt, given out of Judah, Simeon, Benjamin, Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: The children of Issachar were men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do, and their two hundred heads had all their brethren at their commandment.

Issachar's knowledge of the times is why they knew how to sail from the eastern hemisphere to the western, a feat that is no easy thing. When you meet Issachar in the street and speak of the Aztecs and Mayas, bring up their calendars and this verse.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 12: The Tribes Gather to David

points: Many of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun had not cleansed themselves, yet they ate the Passover.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

points: Many of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun eat the Passover otherwise than it was written, but Hezekiah prays that the good Lord pardon everyone who prepares his heart to seek God, and the Lord hearkens and heals the people. Grace and mercy are present here in the Old Testament.
